title: Tiered Traffic Smoothing and Capacity Hedge Guide
author: Asha Menon
content:
Overview:

This guide describes the Tiered Traffic Smoothing and Capacity Hedge system: an operational pattern and accompanying automation for protecting SLOs when inference demand changes rapidly. It codifies detection signals, mitigation tiers, automated and manual actions, verification checks, and post-incident steps. The intent is to reduce full-service outages by gracefully smoothing incoming traffic, preserving critical tenants, and buying time for capacity recovery or routing changes.

Intended audience:
- SREs operating Redwood inference clusters
- Platform engineers implementing autoscale/fallback policies
- Product owners who own SLO contracts and priority tiers

Goals and scope:
- Minimize p99 latency and error-rate SLO violations during surges by applying deterministic, audit-able multi-tier mitigations.
- Introduce capacity hedges that maintain high-priority traffic with bounded degradation for lower tiers.
- Provide an operator playbook for escalations and a set of example configs for automation.
- Excludes long-term capacity procurement decisions, model-level quality regressions, and billing adjustments (handled by finance/product).

Key definitions:
- SLO: the objective for a route or model (e.g., p99 latency < 200ms, availability >= 99.9%).
- Error budget: remaining allowable SLO consumption for a period.
- Capacity headroom: (available serving capacity - baseline allocation) / baseline allocation.
- Hedge: a short-term policy (5–60 minutes) that reduces incoming effective load to prevent further SLO burn.
- Tier: priority class for tenants/requests (tier-0 = system-critical, tier-1 = paid committed, tier-2 = best-effort).

Overview of the strategy:
1) Detect unusual burn or reduced headroom via telemetry.
2) Classify impact by tiers and routes.
3) Apply a sequence of mitigations (smoothing, token-priority, selective throttling, regional spillover).
4) Monitor SLO recovery; escalate or rollback as required.
5) After recovery, run a short retrospective and capture evidence.

Architecture and components:
- Hedge Controller (service): reads telemetry, evaluates policies, emits mitigation commands to router and quota services.
- Router (request gateway): enforces per-tenant priority, drop rates, and spillover rules.
- Autoscaler: can be paused/triggered by Hedge Controller to avoid oscillation.
- Observability pipeline: real-time metrics (p50/p95/p99 latency, request success %, burn rate, capacity headroom) and short-lived traces for sample requests.
- Audit log: every mitigation command must be recorded with reason, operator, and correlation id.

Telemetry & primary signals (minimum required):
- p99 latency per-route and per-tenant (1m and 5m sliding windows)
- Request success rate (4xx/5xx) by route and tenant
- Error budget burn rate (1h and 6h) by SLO
- Capacity headroom and active allocation per GPU group
- Queue depth and average dispatch latency in serving runtime
- Token consumption rate and median request token length (embedding/sequence mix)

Trigger thresholds (example policy):
- Tiered alert condition A (warning): capacity headroom < 25% AND p99 > 1.5x SLO for 2 consecutive 1m windows.
- Condition B (escape hatch): error budget burn rate > 3x over 1h and headroom < 15% OR sustained queue depth > 80th percentile for 3 minutes.
- Automated mitigation allowed only when Condition A persists for >= 3 minutes or Condition B triggers.

Tiered mitigations (ordered, shortest impact to longest):
1) Smoothing window (automated): apply request interleaving with 20–100ms per-tenant jitter and client-side retry guidance to reduce microbursts.
2) Token-priority weighting (automated): reduce per-request token limit for tier-2 by configurable factor (default 0.6x).
3) Soft throttling (automated): apply token-based rate limits to tier-2 and optional non-critical routes (example: 50% of baseline).
4) Spillover routing (semi-automated): route tier-1 traffic to alternate region or dedicated reserve cluster. Requires autoscaler freeze and confirmation from operator for cross-region costs.
5) Reject with helpful payload (manual/automated): return HTTP 429 with structured JSON explaining degradation and suggested retry-after.
6) Emergency admission control (manual): toggle tenant eviction policies as last resort.

Operational runbook: detection and immediate response
1) Alert fires (Condition A or B). Pager to oncall SRE with short context (affected routes, top tenants, headroom).
2) Oncall reviews dashboard: global headroom, p99 map, top 10 tenants by RPS, and recent deploys.
3) If Condition A: enable smoothing window (Hedge Controller) and set token-priority for tier-2. Document action in incident channel.
4) If Condition B: escalate to Tier 2 mitigation (soft throttling) and prepare spillover plan. Notify Product for possible rate-limiting of non-critical flows.
5) Monitor for 5 minutes; if p99 trends back toward SLO and error budget burn normalizes, gradually roll mitigations back (reverse order).
6) If mitigations fail after 15 minutes, invoke regional spillover and notify exec oncall.

Automated hedging configuration (example YAML):

# Hedge Controller policy example
policy_name: "tiered-smoothing-default"
windows:
  - name: "fast"
    duration: "1m"
    criteria:
      headroom_pct: 25
      p99_multiplier: 1.5
    actions:
      - type: "smoothing"
        jitter_ms: 50
      - type: "token_priority"
        tier: "tier-2"
        multiplier: 0.6
  - name: "urgent"
    duration: "3m"
    criteria:
      headroom_pct: 15
      burn_rate: 3
    actions:
      - type: "soft_throttle"
        tiers: ["tier-2"]
        throttle_ratio: 0.5
      - type: "spillover"
        target: "reserve-cluster-us-west-2"
        require_manual_approval: true

(Place this YAML under /etc/hedger/policies/*.yaml in the cluster. Hedge Controller validates schema and performs dry-run before apply.)

Verification and safety checks:
- Canary the mitigation on < 1% of traffic for 30s before global apply (default).
- Enforce automations only when a quorum of telemetry sources agree (metrics pipeline, runtime queue feed, and router queue).
- Ensure circuit-breaker anti-flapping: once a mitigation is applied, do not roll it back for at least 90s and do not reapply the same mitigation more than 3 times in 10 minutes.
- All automated actions must include correlation-id and the triggering signal stored in the audit log.

Rollback and escalation guidance:
- Immediate rollback: if SLOs worsen within two full sampling windows (2m) after applying a mitigation, reverse the last action and escalate to senior SRE.
- Manual escalation path: oncall -> SRE lead -> Platform eng -> Product (if customer-visible throttle). Use incident channel #sre-hedges and open an incident ticket with the hedge audit id.

Post-incident checklist (within 48 hours):
- Attach hedge audit id to incident ticket and capture: triggers, actions, timeline, and operator notes.
- Export telemetry snapshots (1h before, during, 1h after) and retain for 90 days.
- Run a root-cause hypothesis session with platform and runtime teams.
- If a capacity shortage is recurrent, add a Capacity Remediation ticket (owner: infra-capacity) with recommended procurement or autoscaler tuning.

Dashboards and alerts to create:
- Hedge Controller status: last action, active mitigations, recent reversals
- Per-route SLO health with tier breakdown (p50/p95/p99 + success%)
- Capacity headroom heatmap by GPU cluster and availability zone
- Top tenants by error budget burn and token consumption
- Alert: "hedge-auto-apply" when automated mitigation executes (include diff of policy applied)

Audit and compliance requirements:
- Persist all mitigations and decisions in audit store for at least 365 days.
- Include operator identity, trigger signals, mitigation diffs, and revert reasons.
- For customer-impacting hedges (tier-1 throttles or rejects), notify customer-success and log the incident in the customer-facing incident tracker.

Ownership and SLAs:
- Hedge Controller owner: eng-sre/operational-tooling team (primary).
- Autoscaler: eng-infra (secondary).
- Post-incident review owner: oncall SRE for the incident.
- Expected response times: initial stabilization action within 5 minutes of Condition B; full incident resolution or escalation within 30 minutes.

Examples and CLI snippets:
- Apply policy dry-run:
  ./hedgerctl apply --policy tiered-smoothing-default --dry-run --cluster us-west-2
- Inspect active mitigations:
  ./hedgerctl status --cluster us-west-2 --output json
- Revert mitigation by id:
  ./hedgerctl revert --id hedge-20270208-0042 --reason "rollback after latency regression"

Metrics to include in postmortem template:
- p99 latency (route/tenant) 5m windows
- error budget consumed (1h, 24h)
- capacity headroom timeline
- mitigation timeline with hedge audit ids

References and related docs:

Appendix: sample 429 payload for helpful failures
{
  "code": "SERVICE_DEGRADED",
  "message": "Service is temporarily throttling non-critical requests to preserve latency for critical traffic. See retry-after and tier info.",
  "retry_after_seconds": 30,
  "tier_action": "soft_throttle",
  "audit_id": "hedge-20270208-0042"
}
